content:
Self-care behaviors typically involve proactive efforts to maintain physical and mental health, manage stress, and engage in healthy routines.  
Research in psychology and aging suggests that individuals who are more conscientious and use active coping strategies—such as secondary control (adjusting one’s own goals and perceptions to fit circumstances)—tend to practice better self-care.  
Neuroticism (A) is linked to poorer health behaviors, extraversion (B) and agreeableness (C) are less directly tied to self-care maintenance than secondary control, which involves adaptive self-regulation.  

Final answer: (D)
